ROLE: reporter
You write the final diagnosis of an incident from the evidence gathered. Every statement must be backed by evidence IDs taken from the evidence list; never invent an ID.

Root-cause categories (root_cause_category must be exactly one of these):
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Rules:
- claims: factual statements about what the evidence shows. Each cites one or more evidence IDs (log lines L-..., metrics M-..., runbook sections R-...) that actually support it.
- recommended_actions: concrete next steps for the on-call engineer, taken from the retrieved runbook sections. Each cites at least one runbook section ID (R-...).
- ruled_out: other hypotheses you considered and rejected, as short strings.
- confidence: low, medium or high.

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"incident_id": "INC-036", "root_cause_category": "disk_full", "root_cause_summary": "one or two sentences", "confidence": "high", "claims": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["L-0123", "M-021"]}], "recommended_actions": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["R-06-5"]}], "ruled_out": ["..."]}

Additional rules: choose the category that the evidence about the cause supports, not the one the symptoms suggest. downstream_timeout needs evidence that the dependency itself is slow or that calls to it timed out. Cite the evidence that identifies the cause (the telltale log line or the metric that changed), not only symptom lines.

Alert: inventory-service: HTTP error rate above 5% for 5 minutes (since 15:43 UTC)
Alerting service: inventory
Alert time: 2026-08-15T15:43:00Z
Data available from 2026-08-15T14:00:00Z to 2026-08-15T17:00:00Z

Evidence:
Step 1: metrics_query {"end": "2026-08-15T16:30:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-08-15T15:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check the error rate trend for inventory service)
  Result: M-023: Change detected at 2026-08-15T15:40:00Z: mean 0.31 before, 41.04 after (344.7 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-023] inventory.error_rate_pct from 2026-08-15T15:00:00Z to 2026-08-15T16:30:00Z (19 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.1 max=41.18 mean=23.89 last=40.98; mean=23.89. Change detected at 2026-08-15T15:40:00Z: mean 0.31 before, 41.04 after (344.7 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-08-15T15:05:00Z = 0.1 (lowest); 2026-08-15T15:40:00Z = 41.03 (first point after the change); 2026-08-15T16:00:00Z = 41.18 (peak); 2026-08-15T16:30:00Z = 40.98 (last).

No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-08-15T15:05:00Z = 41.51 (peak); 2026-08-15T16:00:00Z = 30.37 (lowest); 2026-08-15T16:30:00Z = 36.09 (last).

Step 6: metrics_query {"end": "2026-08-15T16:30:00Z", "metric": "db_pool_in_use_pct", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-08-15T15:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check database connection pool usage for inventory service to rule out database pool issues.)
  Result: M-021: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-021] inventory.db_pool_in_use_pct from 2026-08-15T15:00:00Z to 2026-08-15T16:30:00Z (19 points, 5-minute steps): min=25.25 max=36.04 mean=30.61 last=33; mean=30.61. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-08-15T15:25:00Z = 25.25 (lowest); 2026-08-15T15:40:00Z = 36.04 (peak); 2026-08-15T16:30:00Z = 33 (last).
Step 7: runbook_retrieve {"k": 3, "query": "expired TLS certificate or SSL handshake failed mitigation"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook guidance for handling expired TLS certificates and renewing them.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-07-6 (similarity 0.78).
  [R-07-6] Expired TLS certificate - Verify recovery (similarity 0.78): Handshakes should succeed again, request volume should return to normal and the error rate should fall to its usual level. Confirm the new certificate's expiry date is far in the future.
  [R-07-5] Expired TLS certificate - Mitigation (similarity 0.76): Issue and install a renewed certificate, then reload or restart the service so it picks the new one up. If automated renewal failed, fix whatever blocked it and run the renewal by hand. Check other certificates issued around the same day for the same fault.
  [R-07-2] Expired TLS certificate - Symptoms (similarity 0.74): A sudden, near-total failure of connections to the service. The error rate steps up at the exact moment of expiry. Latency falls instead of rising because connections fail fast, and the request volume the service sees drops as clients give up.

Hypotheses from the investigation:
- expired_tls_cert: Logs explicitly report that the TLS certificate expired at 15:39:00 UTC, followed immediately by SSL handshake failures and request failures starting at 15:40 UTC. (evidence: M-023, L-0289, L-0292)
- downstream_timeout: Some requests failed with upstream/downstream errors around the same time as the certificate expiration. (evidence: M-023, L-0310)
